Package frc.spectrumLib.vision

Class Limelight

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.vision.Limelight
public class Limelight extends Object
Wraps one Limelight camera for AprilTag pose estimation and basic targeting.

Every getter is safe on a detached camera (isAttached() is false) and returns zero, false, or an empty value.

Getters share one NetworkTables sample per robot loop. The first getter to need a topic reads it, and every later getter in that loop reuses the sample, so pose, tag count, fiducials, and timestamp all describe the same camera frame. The owning subsystem calls invalidate() once per loop before any getter. Returned LimelightHelpers.PoseEstimate and LimelightHelpers.RawFiducial objects belong to that sample and must not be mutated.

MegaTag1 solves pose from the tags alone. MegaTag2 fuses in the heading the owning subsystem passes to setRobotOrientation(double).

    • pushConfiguredCameraPose

      public void pushConfiguredCameraPose()
      Writes the configured mount offsets (Limelight.LimelightConfig.withTranslation(double, double, double) and Limelight.LimelightConfig.withRotation(double, double, double)) to the camera, so the code is the source of truth instead of the values typed into the web UI. The six values cross in the order and sign the camera wants, so a config value can be read straight against the matching web UI box.

      A camera keeps its own copy in flash and falls back to it on boot, so this has to run again periodically: one that reboots mid-match reverts to whatever was last typed into it. See the resend loop in Vision.periodic(). Does not flush NetworkTables.

    • setRobotOrientation

      public void setRobotOrientation(double degrees, double angularRate)
      Sets the heading and yaw rate the camera's internal IMU fuses, for MegaTag2.

      Does not flush NetworkTables. The owning subsystem flushes once after all per-loop writes.

      Parameters:
      degrees - robot heading in degrees, positive counter-clockwise
      angularRate - current yaw rate in degrees per second
